segments.text: Summer Morning by John Clear Read for LibriVox.org by Marianne Coleman-Hipkins
www.thisvoiceforyou.com The cocks have now been mournful told,
The sun again begins to peep, The shepherd whistling to his fold,
Unpins and frees, the captive sheep, Old pathless plains at early hours,
the sleepy rustic slumigoes. The twos brushed off from grass and flowers be moistening
sopp his hardened shoes. While every leaf that forms a shade and every flower it's
silken top and every shivering bent end blade stoops bowing with a diamond drop.
but soon shall fly those diamond drops, the red round sun at advance is higher,
and stretching off the mountain tops is gilding sweet, the village spire,
it is sweet to meet the morning breeze, or list the gurgling of the brook, or
stretched beneath the shade of trees, peruse and to pause on nature's book.
when nature every switch prepares to entertain our wished delay. The images
which morning wears, the wakening chums of early day, now let me tread the
meadow path while glittering to the groundy looms, as sprinkled over the
wuthering spots, the moisture shrinks and sweet perfumes, and hear the beetle
little sound his horn, and hear the sky-lark whistling nigh, sprung from his bed of tufted
corn, a hailey minstrel from the sky, and of poem, this recording is in the public domain.
